title: What each ZMS GraphQL query takes and returns: agents, resources, groups, rules, zones, catalog, tags

prose.text: Each ZMS domain has one or more queries; the selection set written in the SDK module is what comes back, since the methods return the raw GraphQL result ([[zms.api:raw-dicts]]).

prose.label: Values.
prose.text: Enum values and filter inputs are in [[zms.api.enums-and-filters]].

stats-unpaged.statement: The agent connection-status and version statistics queries take only `customerId` and an optional `search`, with no pagination, and return totals with per-type rows.

quotes: query AgentConnectionStatusStats($customerId: ID!, $search: String) { agentConnectionStatusStatistics( customerId: $customerId, search: $search ) { totalCount totalPercentage agentStatuses { agentType connectionStatus count percentage } } }

query AgentVersionStats($customerId: ID!, $search: String) { agentVersionStatistics( customerId: $customerId, search: $search ) { totalCount totalPercentage agentVersions { agentType version count percentage } } }

agents-selection.statement: The agents list selects name, eyezId, connectionStatus, agentType, hostOs, currentSoftwareVersion, upgradeStatus, description, cloudProvider, publicIp, privateIps, adminStatus, agentGroupName and agentGroupType, and accepts search, sort and sortDir.

quotes: nodes { name eyezId connectionStatus agentType hostOs currentSoftwareVersion upgradeStatus description cloudProvider publicIp privateIps adminStatus agentGroupName agentGroupType }
search: $search, sort: $sort, sortDir: $sortDir

agent-groups-selection.statement: The agent groups list selects name, eyezId, agentGroupType, cloudProvider, adminStatus, agentCount, description, policyStatus, upgradeStatus, tamperProtectionStatus, agentAutoUpgrade, agentDeletionTimeoutSeconds, timezone, upgradeDay, upgradeTime and versionProfileName.

quotes: nodes { name eyezId agentGroupType cloudProvider adminStatus agentCount description policyStatus upgradeStatus tamperProtectionStatus agentAutoUpgrade agentDeletionTimeoutSeconds timezone upgradeDay upgradeTime versionProfileName }

totp-secrets.statement: `agentGroupTotpSecrets`, keyed by an agent group's eyezId, returns `totpSecret`, `totpQrCode` and `totpGenerationTimestamp`.

quotes: agentGroupTotpSecrets(customerId: $customerId, eyezId: $eyezId) { eyezId totpSecret totpQrCode totpGenerationTimestamp }

resources-selection.statement: The resources list selects id, name, resourceType, status, cloudProvider, cloudRegion, resourceHostname, platformOs, platformOsDistro, platformOsVersion, localIps, deleted, modifiedTime, agentId, appZoneIds, appZoneNames and appZoneMappingState.

quotes: nodes { id name resourceType status cloudProvider cloudRegion resourceHostname platformOs platformOsDistro platformOsVersion localIps deleted modifiedTime agentId appZoneIds appZoneNames appZoneMappingState }

include-deleted.statement: The resources query takes `includeDeleted` (`include_deleted`, default False), so deleted resources are left out unless asked for.

quotes: include_deleted: bool = False,
includeDeleted: $includeDeleted,

protection-status.statement: Resource and resource-group protection status queries take `pageNum` and `pageSize` and return `nodes` of protected percentage and protected, unprotected and total counts, with a `pageInfo` block.

quotes: resourceProtectionStatus( customerId: $customerId, pageNum: $pageNum, pageSize: $pageSize ) {
nodes { protectedPercentage protectedResourcesCount unprotectedResourcesCount totalResources } pageInfo {
resourceGroupProtectionStatus( customerId: $customerId, pageNum: $pageNum, pageSize: $pageSize ) {
nodes { protectedPercentage protectedResourceGroupsCount unprotectedResourceGroupsCount totalResourceGroups } pageInfo {

metadata-scalar.statement: `metadata` takes only the customer ID and the query selects no subfields; the SDK documents `get_metadata` as getting event metadata for a customer, returned as metadata JSON.

quotes: query GetMetadata($customerId: String!) { metadata(customerId: $customerId) }
Get event metadata for a customer.
tuple: (metadata JSON, response, error)
def get_metadata(

group-fragments.statement: `resourceGroups` returns two concrete types through inline fragments: `ManagedResourceGroup` with id, name, description, type, origin, resourceMemberCount and modifiedTime, and `UnmanagedResourceGroup` with the same plus `cidrs` and `fqdns`.

quotes: resourceGroups( customerId: $customerId, pageNum: $pageNum, pageSize: $pageSize, filter: $filter ) { nodes { ... on ManagedResourceGroup { id name description type origin resourceMemberCount modifiedTime } ... on UnmanagedResourceGroup { id name description type origin resourceMemberCount modifiedTime cidrs fqdns } }

group-membership.statement: Managed groups have tag-based membership and unmanaged groups CIDR- or FQDN-based membership.

quotes: **Resource groups have two types**: `ManagedResourceGroup` (tag-based membership) and `UnmanagedResourceGroup` (CIDR/FQDN-based).

group-members.statement: `resourceGroupMembers` is keyed by the group's `id` (`String!`) and pages with `pageNum` and `pageSize`.

quotes: query GetResourceGroupMembers( $customerId: ID!, $id: String!, $pageNum: Int, $pageSize: Int )

policy-rules-selection.statement: Policy rules select id, name, action, priority, description, deleted, source, destination and AppZone-scope target types, creationTime, modifiedTime, lastHit and port ranges per protocol.

quotes: nodes { id name action priority description deleted sourceTargetType destinationTargetType appZoneScopeTargetType creationTime modifiedTime lastHit portAndProtocols { protocol portRanges { startPort endPort } } }

default-rules-selection.statement: Default policy rules are a separate query, paginated with no filter or fetchAll, selecting id, name, action, direction, description, scopeType and modifiedTime.

quotes: query ListDefaultPolicyRules( $customerId: ID!, $pageNum: Int, $pageSize: Int ) { defaultPolicyRules( customerId: $customerId, pageNum: $pageNum, pageSize: $pageSize ) { nodes { id name action direction description scopeType modifiedTime }

app-zones-selection.statement: App zones take a filter and orderBy and select id, appZoneName, description, memberCount, includeAllVpcs and includeAllSubnets.

quotes: nodes { id appZoneName description memberCount includeAllVpcs includeAllSubnets }
$filter: AppZoneFilter, $orderBy: AppZoneQueryOrderBy

app-catalog-selection.statement: App catalog entries select id, name, category, creationTime, modifiedTime and details of port ranges per protocol and processes.

quotes: nodes { id name category creationTime modifiedTime details { portAndProtocol { protocol portRanges { startPort endPort } } processes } }

tag-hierarchy.statement: Tags are walked top-down: `tagNamespaces` lists namespaces (id, name, description, origin), `tagKeys` needs a `namespaceId`, and `tagValues` needs both a `tagId` and a `namespaceOrigin` of type `NamespaceOrigin!`.

quotes: Tag hierarchy is three levels: namespace → key → value. Navigate top-down to list tag values.
tagNamespaces( customerId: $customerId, pageNum: $pageNum, pageSize: $pageSize, filter: $filter, orderBy: $orderBy ) { nodes { id name description origin }
tagKeys( customerId: $customerId, namespaceId: $namespaceId,
$namespaceId: String!
$tagId: String!, $namespaceOrigin: NamespaceOrigin!

metadata-returns-scalar.statement: `metadata` returns a scalar value rather than an object type.
metadata-returns-scalar.conditions: Rests on the GraphQL rule that a field queried without a selection set must be a leaf (scalar or enum) type; the ZMS schema itself is not captured, so the scalar's name and shape are unknown.
